So I've been watching this story about this school in Wisconsin. You may have seen it under such scary titles as 'Parents Push Religion at â€˜Jesus Lunchesâ€™ at Wisconsin High School' and 'Middleton school officials ask parents to stop 'Jesus Lunch' events', but few articles mention a few super-dooper important things about this situation.

Once a week, parents from the neighborhood will make home-cooked meals and bring them to this publicly owned park across from the school and offer free lunches to the high school kids (who are allowed to leave campus for lunch). The kids have access not only to the delicious school lunches, but there is also a McDonald's and a Taco Bell nearby (I am told - I haven't google-mapped it or anything.). They have lots of places to go. But these parents rent out a pavilion in this publicly owned park and offer free lunches.

The catch? They talk about God and Christianity while you are there.

And this is just so traumatizing for school students. This thing they don't have to attend it just so close to the school, school officials have sent letters to the parents telling them to stop and demanded that the city make them stop using the public park for events open to the public. They've even made a lame attempt to stop them - with traffic cones.

Now look - I get it. People don't want religion in school. And that's fine. I'm not religious, I don't get why people do this, but I understand the desire to share something you like with other people. And that's what these parents are doing. They make free food, they feed it to kids, and all they ask is that you be respectful while they talk about something they're passionate about. It's the same thing they do at those political dinners, world summits, art shows, school plays, etc. etc. - We are giving away something good for free and just want a little of your time. It's a fair exchange and not harming anyone.

One of those articles had some blurb about how some kids 'felt left out' because they weren't religious. Hate to be the one to say it, but that's fine. There are going to be things in the world you don't like, you don't want to do, and it makes you feel left out because someone else likes it and wants to do it. That is life, little friend. In all seriousness, the kid's shouldn't feel left out at all. The parents with the free food are just talking, not asking for blood on a document. Have you ever gone to the mall to go shopping and had to listen to holiday music? Yeah, that shit's annoying. But you tolerate it because you are getting something out of it - the ability to shop for what you want. This is the same thing. You don't have to be Christmas shopping to go to the mall in December. You don't have to be religious to enjoy the food. There is nothing that says 'Only Christians Can Eat Here'.

It's not like this lunch is run by BLM or other diversity groups. Literally everyone is welcome.

Because.
